base_instruction: You are a helpful catering and event planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a retirement party by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're throwing a retirement party for our department head Dave next Friday. I'm in charge of catering — can you help me figure out the food?

flow_info.value: Confirmed attendees so far: me, Dave (the retiree), Susan, Marcus, and Priya
Susan was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Marcus ate shrimp at the company picnic last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
We booked the rooftop terrace at the office building, capacity 30 but we're expecting around 12-15
Budget is about 25 dollars per head, so maybe 350 total
Dave's wife Helen is coming too, she's been doing keto for the past six months
Priya just told me she got called to the client site that day, so she can't make it. She asked if I could save her a plate though
Marcus texted me — turns out his allergist confirmed it was a one-time reaction to contaminated shrimp, not an actual shellfish allergy. He's been eating seafood fine since then
Oh and Tony from accounting is coming, he just confirmed
What time should we set up the food — like 11:30 for a noon start, or earlier?

The caterer sent over their party platter options: Caesar salad with croutons, pesto pasta, Worcestershire-glazed meatballs, coconut shrimp, and a veggie crudité platter with hummus. Any issues with these for our group?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Susan was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.surface_form: Marcus ate shrimp at the company picnic last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen use → anaphylactic allergic reaction

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up in a strict Jain household in Gujarat and still follows all the practices
inference_chain: Strict Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato)

constraints.value: Following keto diet — avoids high-carb foods like bread, pasta, rice, sugar
constraints.surface_form: Dave's wife Helen has been doing keto for the past six months
inference_chain: Keto diet → very low carbohydrate intake
Avoids bread, pasta, rice, sugar, starchy foods

constraints.value: Allergic to tree nuts — cannot eat pine nuts, walnuts, almonds, cashews, pistachios, etc.
constraints.surface_form: Tony carries an EpiPen everywhere because of tree nuts. His last reaction was from a walnut brownie at a potluck
inference_chain: EpiPen for tree nuts → severe tree nut allergy
Tree nuts include walnuts, almonds, pine nuts, cashews, pistachios, etc.

hidden_state.value: You are organizing catering for a retirement party. You will introduce attendees and their backgrounds across several turns. People will join and leave. At the end you will share a specific menu from the caterer and ask if there are any issues. You do NOT know the answers yourself — you genuinely want the assistant to check.

You are a calm, cooperative office organizer. You always refer to colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Marcus texted me...', 'Susan told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal event coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: Caesar salad problematic for Susan (croutons contain gluten); pesto pasta problematic for Susan (pasta is wheat/gluten) AND for Helen (high carb) AND contains pine nuts problematic for Tony; Worcestershire-glazed meatballs contain hidden anchovy (Worcestershire sauce is made with anchovies — fish) so cannot go on Priya's saved plate; coconut shrimp is fine (Marcus cleared, coconut is not a tree nut); veggie crudité with hummus is fine for everyone at the table
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Caesar salad with croutons: problematic for Susan (celiac — croutons are made from bread, which contains gluten). Pesto pasta: problematic for Susan (pasta is wheat-based, contains gluten), problematic for Helen (pasta is high-carb, violates keto), and problematic for Tony (traditional pesto contains pine nuts, which are tree nuts). Worcestershire-glazed meatballs: the Worcestershire sauce is made with anchovies (fish) — this means it cannot be included on Priya's saved plate (Jain diet forbids fish); fine for the table since Priya is not attending in person. Coconut shrimp: fine for everyone — Marcus's shellfish concern was cleared by his allergist, and coconut is a fruit, not a tree nut. Veggie crudité platter with hummus: fine for everyone at the table and can be included on Priya's saved plate.
required_elements: Caesar salad with croutons is problematic for Susan because croutons contain gluten and she has celiac disease
Pesto pasta is problematic for Susan because pasta contains gluten
Pesto pasta is problematic for Helen because pasta is high-carb and she follows keto
Pesto pasta is problematic for Tony because traditional pesto contains pine nuts which are tree nuts
Worcestershire-glazed meatballs cannot be included on Priya's saved plate because Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies (fish) and Priya follows strict Jain diet which forbids fish
Coconut shrimp is fine — Marcus's shellfish allergy was cleared by his allergist
Veggie crudité platter with hummus is fine for everyone
forbidden_elements: Flagging coconut shrimp as problematic for Marcus (his allergy was confirmed to not be real)
Flagging coconut shrimp as problematic for Tony (coconut is not a tree nut)
Completely rejecting Worcestershire-glazed meatballs for the table (only problematic for Priya's saved plate, fine for in-person attendees)
Flagging any item for Priya as if she is attending in person (she is not coming, only needs a saved plate)
Saying Marcus still has a shellfish allergy
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking, inferential constraint reasoning, and hidden ingredient detection across 9 turns. Key challenges: (1) Susan has celiac → gluten-free (inferential), affecting croutons and pasta. (2) Marcus's shellfish allergy is REMOVED mid-conversation (allergist cleared it) — coconut shrimp is now fine. (3) Priya EXITS but needs a saved plate — her Jain constraint (no meat, fish, eggs, root vegetables) applies only to the saved plate. (4) Helen JOINS with keto constraint — pasta is high-carb. (5) Tony JOINS late with tree nut allergy — pesto contains pine nuts (hidden ingredient trap). (6) The primary hidden ingredient trap: Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies (fish), which violates Priya's Jain diet for her saved plate. Most people don't know Worcestershire sauce is made with fermented anchovies. (7) Coconut shrimp is a trap item — looks problematic (shellfish for Marcus, 'coconut' sounds like tree nut for Tony) but is actually fine for everyone since Marcus is cleared and coconut is botanically a fruit/drupe, not a tree nut.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
